Notify: the coalescing flake is test-only at its root. The test's probe uses `>=` while the product's `isFreshnessStale` uses `>`, so a same-millisecond install reads stale only in the test. Filed and dispatched as cloud#3836 (p2). The test will call `isFreshnessStale` on a controlled clock. The card also measures the product side: whether `>` can miss a same-millisecond write after the content read. Until it lands, a re-run is the fair answer.

Several writers put the freshness marker in the same update as the change they stamp, before that change commits: `org-plan.ts:365`, `domains.ts:704`, `organization-lifecycle.ts:809`, `environment-lifecycle/context.ts:297`, `transitions.ts:159/214`. A build that starts between the stamp and the commit reads the old state with `builtAtMs` after the stamp, so no probe comparison can see it. Separately, cloud#3841 (armed) makes `isFreshnessStale` `>=`, so stamp-equal post-commit changes are no longer missed. Card it if you agree.
